activities.caption: compute the neuron — then check it
activities.name: nfxNeuronEstimate

config.prompt: Inputs x₁ = 2 and x₂ = 3; weights w₁ = 0.5 and w₂ = −0.25; bias b = 1. What is the weighted sum?
config.why: 2 × 0.5 + 3 × (−0.25) + 1 = 1.25 — ReLU passes it through as 1.25; a sigmoid would squash it to ≈ 0.78. That is the entire neuron: a linear score, bent by a squish.
config.context: The weights are the knowledge: w₁ = 0.5 says 'input 1 speaks positively'; w₂ = −0.25 says 'input 2 speaks against'; the bias shifts the firing threshold.

activities.anchor: the trained network understands the data
activities.caption: file the claims — what training does and doesn't do
activities.name: nfxTrainBuckets

config.prompt: Two misconceptions, one sorter — file each claim:

items.label: adjusts numbers to minimise a loss score on the examples seen
exploits whatever patterns correlate with the labels
stops in the first good valley of the loss landscape it finds
endows the network with understanding of the data
finds the single true answer to compare yours against

config.why: A different random seed usually lands in a different valley — several good solutions generalise similarly, and there is rarely a single 'true' answer.

activities.caption: drag the divider — wide versus deep
activities.name: nfxWideCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to spend parameters — drag between them:

before.label: Wide (one huge hidden layer)
before.text: Universal approximation: enough neurons can approximate any continuous function to any precision — but parameter-hungry.

after.label: Deep (many small layers)
after.text: Composition reuses features — complicated functions with far fewer parameters, and learned better: that is why 'deep' learning is deep.

config.why: Depth's advantage is practical rather than absolute — Cybenko (1989) and Hornik (1991) proved one hidden layer suffices in principle.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — why the GPU was waiting
activities.name: nfxMatrixCloze

config.text: Organised as matrices, the whole layer step is one %%0%% plus one %%1%% — which is why %%2%% (built to multiply matrices for graphics) turned out to be the perfect engine for neural networks.
config.hint: The linear-algebra lesson's machinery is the implementation; the gaming industry built the hardware.

activities.anchor: Gradient descent (the optimisation lesson's subject) says
activities.caption: rebuild the training loop, forward to nudge
activities.name: nfxLoopOrder

config.prompt: Training is just the loop — put it in order:
items: forward pass — push the example through the layers
loss — score the prediction against the truth
backward pass — the chain rule assigns every weight its gradient
nudge every weight a small step opposite its gradient
repeat over batches of examples for many epochs
config.why: Each layer's backward work is reused by all layers before it — one backward pass, output to input, computes every weight's gradient. At billions of weights, 'nudge repeatedly' is exactly how the astonishing capabilities get built.

activities.caption: true or false — the depth dial
activities.name: nfxDepthJudge

statements.s: Depth adds expressive power but also vanishing gradients, longer training and overfitting risk.
statements.why: Capacity must match the data — depth is a dial, not a virtue.
Many real problems are solved better by three layers tuned carefully than thirty tuned carelessly.

statements.s: The validation set — not ambition — decides the right capacity.
statements.why: Which is why the train-versus-test gap, not layer count, is the diagnosis.

statements.s: A network that scores brilliantly on training data has proved its depth was right.
statements.why: Near-perfect training scores are the signature of memorisation — the honest number lives on data the network never saw.

activities.anchor: The settings you choose before training
activities.caption: which loss curve is the healthy learning rate?
activities.name: nfxRateTrace

config.prompt: Three learning rates, three loss curves over training steps. Which one is healthy?
config.why: Too high and the loss oscillates or explodes (divergence); too low and it crawls — which is why loss curves are plotted live and the learning rate is the first thing to check when training misbehaves.

activities.anchor: The countermeasures form a standard kit
activities.caption: pair each countermeasure with its mechanism
activities.name: nfxRegMatch

config.prompt: The regularisation kit — pair each tool with how it fights memorisation:

pairs.right: randomly silence a fraction of neurons each step — no neuron can rely on a particular partner
penalise large weights, biasing toward simpler functions
stop when validation loss rises while training loss keeps falling
enlarge the training set with label-preserving transformations — often the highest-yield of all

config.why: The train-versus-test gap is the symptom; the gap's direction tells you which disease you have.
